A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe SpectroMotion. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching content despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original NeRF-DS and HyperNeRF reconstruction experiments, quantitative ablations, and qualitative rendering results.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds component comparisons, parameter sensitivity results, and training and rendering measurements.

M1.justification: The stated specular-color computation is locally revised: v1 multiplies specular color by s_tint in Eq. 11; v2 explicitly uses s_tint*F1+F2 in the split-sum BRDF and adds the resulting specular color directly. This changes the documented shading formulation. Deformation networks, physical normal estimation, losses, and staged training remain intact.

E1.justification: Both evaluate seven NeRF-DS scenes and four HyperNeRF scenes, including the same masked specular-object evaluation. Added diagnostics and ablations use retained coverage. Omnidata supplies a pretrained normal estimator for reference visualization rather than an additional evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: The six benchmark comparison methods are retained. V2 Table 6 newly compares the full model with a 2DGS-based representation replacement and a variant using Gaussian shortest axes without physical normal estimation.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce representation and normal-estimation controls, k values of 0, 1, 5, and 50, and normal-loss weights from 0.0001 to 1. V2 also evaluates training time and FPS. Existing image-quality metrics and staged training settings remain unchanged; the shared baseline budget is newly disclosed rather than demonstrably changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained stage, loss, and environment-map ablations, v2 directly tests physical normal estimation and a 2DGS replacement (Table 6). Tables 10–11 extend regularization analysis through parameter sweeps. Additional normal/depth diagnostics and efficiency analysis substantially broaden the investigation of geometry, stability, and computational cost.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and dataset averages without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: HyperNeRF results change in v1 Table 3 versus v2 Tables 2/8: SpectroMotion's mean PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS changes from 22.89/0.6672/0.2538 to 22.18/0.6016/0.3143, and Deformable 3DGS changes from 22.16/0.5981/0.3525 to 22.78/0.6201/0.3380. These are revised reported results, without an explanation establishing their cause. V2 also adds substantial component, sensitivity, efficiency, and diagnostic results; NeRF-DS scores and original ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: Sections 3.2.1–3.2.3 revise the mathematical shading specification by explicitly introducing s_tint*F1+F2 and changing the final-color definition. The axis-alignment, rotation, oblateness-based residual, and regularization mathematics remain unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: combining deformation and physically based Gaussian rendering, correcting dynamic normals, deforming environment lighting, and using coarse-to-fine training. The central novelty and performance claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of shortest-axis distortion without physical normal estimation, excessive or insufficient residual regularization, and training collapse at normal-loss weights of at least 0.1. It also qualifies rendering speed by Gaussian count and identifies static rendering baselines as references. The existing dramatic-motion failure limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies Adam and states that all baselines and ablations receive 40,000 iterations. Table 9 adds per-scene training times, FPS, and Gaussian counts. Network architecture, stage timings, cubemap resolution, and GPU information are retained. Conversely, the explicit photometric-loss formula is replaced by a reference to 3DGS.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Omnidata, Relightable 3D Gaussian, and 2D Gaussian Splatting, and removes Zeyu Yang et al.'s real-time dynamic 4D Gaussian work. Its additional published GaussianShader reference identifies an already cited work. The central positioning around dynamic specular reconstruction remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: method motivations are shortened, several displayed equations become inline, and masked-object evaluation and decomposition discussion move into a supplement organized around implementation, results, and limitations. Related-work subsections and the appendix hierarchy are also revised.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout, redesigns Figure 1, and rearranges numerous comparison panels. HyperNeRF receives a main-text summary table with detailed results in the appendix. Existing masked and decomposition displays move, while new normal, sensitivity, component-ablation, and efficiency displays expand the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical diagnosis and practical documentation through direct normal-estimation controls, parameter sensitivity tests, and measured computational costs (Tables 6 and 9–11). These usefully strengthen an already substantial evaluation. The unexplained HyperNeRF result revisions and continued absence of uncertainty estimates limit the overall gain.
